thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx and timeout rate detected in prod-west ingress (error rate 2.3%, p95 latency 1.8s -> 6.2s). Triggered by deploy 2026.03.14-23. Auto-pager -> @maya-nguyen.

maya-nguyen: I'm on it. Acknowledge. Which services are in the path?

jordan-li: sounds like gateway timeouts. I'm seeing spike in gateway->runtime TCP errors in the last 2m.

samir-khan: I can pull logs. Running `curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/query?m=error_rate&env=prod-west&since=5m"` now.

olivia-ops: Support ticket count from prod-west increased — a couple customers reported degraded responses. Notified account reps for a handful of customers.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.14-23 rolled to prod-west at 3412349802 by @jordan-li. Canary passed at 10m.

maya-nguyen: OK rollback readiness check: do we have a safe rollback? Can we pin to 2026.03.14-20?

jordan-li: 2026.03.14-20 is available on dedicated nodes, yes. But need to confirm no schema migrations blocked. I see a surge in request queue depth on the runtime side.

samir-khan: logs: `runtime/serving` shows repeated timeouts with `rpc: context deadline exceeded` and 502 responses from runtime-proxy. Example snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T22:08:12Z] request_id=abc123 status=502 error="rpc: context deadline exceeded" backend=runtime-4 instance=rt-12
[2026-03-14T22:08:12Z] kvcache: miss prefix=":user:session:" key=... latency=4.2s
```

maya-nguyen: That points to either kvcache contention or a kernel-level blocking on a new path. Any change in batching or cache config in the deploy?

jordan-li: The release included an adaptive-batcher tweak and a new fallback path for long contexts. Could be the batcher holding requests longer under certain load shapes.

olivia-ops: Customer-impact quick note: Support flagged 3 enterprise customers with real-time features. SLO alerts for one customer already firing. I'm drafting an outbound.

maya-nguyen: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Scale up runtime pool by +30% in prod-west (temp) 2) If error rate not dropping in 2m, initiate rollback to -20 version. 3) Enable emergency fallback routing to low-latency model variant for affected routes.

samir-khan: Scaling now: `orchestrator scale runtime-prod-west --delta 30% --reason "incident 3412349900"` -> API accepted, adding nodes.

jordan-li: Routing fallback toggle ready: `feature-flag set routing.fallback.lowlatency=true --env prod-west`

maya-nguyen: Doing both. Watch metrics.

(30s pass)

samir-khan: After scaling + fallback, p95 went down from 6.2s -> 2.1s but 5xx still ~1.2% (down from 2.3%). Errors are concentrated on requests with prefix /v1/chat/stream and long contexts > 2048 tokens.

jordan-li: Ok that suggests the new fallback helps short contexts but long-context codepath still misbehaving. I think rollback is necessary. Maya, do you want me to start rollback?

maya-nguyen: Yes please. Initiate rollback to 2026.03.14-20. Communication: post a short note to #general and update status page. Olivia, can you handle the customer comms?

olivia-ops: On it — preparing ETA and guidance.

jordan-li: Rolling back now: `deploy rollback --target 2026.03.14-20 --env prod-west --force --reason "timeout regression after 23"` -> started.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback 2026.03.14-23 -> 2026.03.14-20 initiated at 3412350020 by @jordan-li.

maya-nguyen: Post-rollback watch: keep scaling delta for 5m then scale to normal. Also keep fallback on until we confirm stability.

(90s pass)

samir-khan: Post-rollback metrics: p95 350ms, error rate 0.12%. Good. KV cache latencies back to baseline.

olivia-ops: Sent initial customer update: "We detected a regression after a recent deploy causing timeouts for long-context requests. We rolled back the deploy and are monitoring; no data was lost." Support queue calming.

maya-nguyen: Great. Start incident classification: Sev2 (partial degradation), paging resolved. Collect logs for postmortem: `journalctl -u runtime --since "-15m"` and `telemetry traces for deploy 2026.03.14-23`. Jordan/samir please capture related artifacts and assign a follow-up ticket.

jordan-li: Created issue INF-2026-347: "Adaptive-batcher regression on long contexts" assigned to eng-runtime with priority P0. Included top traces and a diff of the release.

samir-khan: Uploaded logs and flame graphs to the ticket. Noted that an internal default batch timeout went from 3s -> 6s in the new config — likely the culprit.

maya-nguyen: Handoff: I'm unpaged. @jordan-li you own the triage timeline until root cause. Olivia, continue customer comms for the next 2 hours. Support-liaison, please monitor any re-opened tickets.

support-liaison: Acknowledged, monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=resolved (rollback completed and metrics stable). Duration ~4m. Postmortem required.

maya-nguyen: Thanks team. Quick retrospective notes in ticket: avoid changing batch timeout defaults without canarying long-context traffic; add synthetic tests for long-context latency during canary; add automatic rollback threshold for p95>2s within 5m of deploy.

jordan-li: Agreed. I'll schedule a short RFC for safe batching defaults and canary gating.

olivia-ops: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and share a short incident summary with account teams.

maya-nguyen: Closing channel — will reopen if we see regressions. :thumbsup:
